evals.name: novice-hotfix-runbook
evals.prompt: Don't run anything. A teammate who rarely uses git has to merge hotfix/null-currency into mainline next week while I'm out, and other people will be pushing to mainline at the same time. Write merge-runbook.md with the exact git commands in order and what to check before each commit and push, including what to do if the push is rejected.
evals.expected_output: The skill gives a concrete four-phase sequence with --no-ff --no-commit, pull-first, mainline-into-branch-first and a never-force-push rule; a generic runbook often merges the hotfix directly, uses plain `git merge`, or answers a rejected push with --force or a rebase of a shared branch.
expectations: Uses --no-ff and --no-commit
No force push anywhere

Sequence matches the skill: pull mainline, merge mainline into hotfix/null-currency (--no-ff --no-commit), verify, commit, push; then pull mainline, merge hotfix (--no-ff --no-commit), verify, commit, push: Both phases in that order with exact commands
Concrete checks before each commit: git status/diff --cached, resolve conflicts, run build and tests: Checks named per commit with commands
Rejected push handling: pull (merge) mainline again, re-verify, commit, push; explicitly never --force or rebase mainline: Correct recovery and explicit prohibition
Readable for a novice: short steps, real branch names, no unnecessary advanced commands: Copy-pasteable and short

evals.name: protected-main-pr-plan
evals.prompt: Don't run anything, just write the plan. Our repo's default branch is `main` (not mainline) and main is protected on GitHub: nothing lands on it except through a reviewed PR. My branch feature/csv-export is ~40 commits behind main and I already know package-lock.json and src/export/csv.ts will conflict. Write merge-plan.md with the exact git commands, in order, to get feature/csv-export merged, plus how to resolve the lockfile conflict and what to check before each commit and push.
evals.expected_output: A plan that uses main (not mainline), merges main into the feature branch with --no-ff --no-commit, resolves the lockfile by regeneration, and lands through a PR rather than a local merge into main; never force-pushes.
expectations: merge-plan.md uses the real default branch name main and never says mainline
No force push anywhere in merge-plan.md
Updates the feature branch first: fetch/pull main, then merge main into feature/csv-export using --no-ff --no-commit, inspect (git status / git diff --cached), commit, push the feature branch
Lands the change through a pull request into main (open/update a PR, wait for review and checks) and does NOT tell the user to merge feature/csv-export into main locally or push to main directly

Lockfile conflict handled by regenerating it (take one side, e.g. main's package-lock.json, then rerun npm install / npm ci and stage the regenerated file) rather than hand-editing conflict markers in package-lock.json
Concrete checks before each commit and push: no remaining conflict markers, git diff --cached review of src/export/csv.ts, build and tests run
If the push or PR shows the branch is behind again, repeats the main-into-branch merge rather than force-pushing or rebasing a shared branch

scripted_checks.text: merge-plan.md uses the real default branch name main and never says mainline
scripted_checks.check: test -s merge-plan.md && grep -q 'main' merge-plan.md && ! grep -qi 'mainline' merge-plan.md

scripted_checks.text: No force push anywhere in merge-plan.md

evals.name: half-done-merge-recovery
evals.prompt: Don't run anything, just write the steps. Yesterday I ran `git merge feature/rate-limit` while on mainline, got conflicts in Cargo.lock and src/limiter.rs, and walked away; `git status` still says 'You have unmerged paths'. Our team merges locally into mainline (no PRs) and others push to mainline all day. Write recover-merge.md with the exact git commands, in order, to get out of this half-done merge and land feature/rate-limit on mainline properly, including how to handle the Cargo.lock conflict and what to check before each commit and push.
evals.expected_output: Backs out with git merge --abort (or finishes deliberately), then redoes it the skill's way: pull mainline, merge mainline into feature/rate-limit with --no-ff --no-commit, resolve, check, commit, push; then merge the feature into mainline with --no-ff --no-commit, review, push. Cargo.lock is regenerated, not hand-edited; no force push.
expectations: recover-merge.md uses git merge --abort to back out of the half-done merge
No force push anywhere in recover-merge.md
Redoes the merge with --no-ff --no-commit and merges mainline into feature/rate-limit first (after pulling mainline), committing and pushing the feature branch before merging it into mainline

Cargo.lock conflict is resolved by taking one side and regenerating it with cargo (e.g. cargo generate-lockfile, cargo update -w, or cargo build), then staging it, rather than hand-editing conflict markers
Concrete checks before each commit: git status shows no unmerged paths, git diff --cached --check or a conflict-marker search, reading the diff of src/limiter.rs, and cargo build plus cargo test

Before pushing to mainline, reviews what will be pushed (e.g. git log --oneline and git diff --stat origin/mainline..HEAD) and pulls/merges origin/mainline again if the push is rejected, never rebasing or force-pushing
Stays focused on the merge: does not add release tagging or branch deletion steps the user did not ask for

scripted_checks.text: recover-merge.md uses git merge --abort to back out of the half-done merge
No force push anywhere in recover-merge.md

evals.name: shared-branch-rejected-push
evals.prompt: Don't run anything, just write the steps. My coworker and I both push to feature/billing-retry. I merged mainline into it with --no-ff --no-commit, committed, and then `git push origin feature/billing-retry` was rejected as non-fast-forward because my coworker pushed two commits to feature/billing-retry an hour ago. Our team merges locally into mainline (no PRs) and I'll run your steps myself. Write next-steps.md with the exact git commands, in order, to get my push through and then land feature/billing-retry on mainline, and what to check before each commit and push.
evals.expected_output: Recovers the rejected feature-branch push by fetching and merging origin/feature/billing-retry (the coworker's commits), re-checking and pushing, never rebasing or force-pushing the shared branch; then pulls mainline, merges the feature with --no-ff --no-commit, checks, commits, reviews log and diff stat, and asks for explicit confirmation before pushing mainline.
expectations: No force push anywhere in next-steps.md

Recovers the rejected push by integrating the coworker's commits on the same branch: fetch then merge origin/feature/billing-retry (or git pull origin feature/billing-retry without --rebase), rather than only merging origin/mainline again
Does not rebase or reset feature/billing-retry (no git rebase, git pull --rebase, or git reset --hard on the shared branch) and says why: the coworker already has that history
After the recovery merge, runs the pre-commit checks before committing and pushing: git status shows no unmerged paths, git diff --cached (or --check) is reviewed, and build plus tests run
Lands on mainline the skill's way: switch to mainline and pull, git merge --no-ff --no-commit feature/billing-retry, checks, commit with a message naming the branch
Before git push to mainline, shows what will be pushed (git log --oneline and/or git diff --stat origin/mainline..HEAD) and tells the user to stop and explicitly confirm before pushing mainline
Stays focused on the merge: does not add release tagging or branch deletion steps the user did not ask for

scripted_checks.text: No force push anywhere in next-steps.md
